sections.h2: Douglas County offices that touch your bill
sections.html:
The county splits the work between an appraisal team and an elected collector. Appraisal sets values and handles appeals for the Board of Assessors. The Tax Commissioner bills, collects and takes homestead forms, and the commissioner's website explains the bill, notices, exemptions and the delinquent list.

  • Appraisal Department: write to 8700 Hospital Dr., Douglasville, GA 30134 or call 770-920-7228. Walk-in filing is on the annex's second floor at 6200 Fairburn Rd.
  • Tax Commissioner: ground-level office in the Government Annex, open to the public on weekdays with a closure at noon for lunch.
  • Finance Department: publishes millage rate documents and hearing dates.

Field appraisers also canvass neighborhoods. Their visits cover permit follow-up, new construction, additions, remodels, sales, appeals and returns, with measuring and photographing along the way. Each wears a photo badge and drives a marked vehicle.

sections.h2: Assessment notices and the filing deadline
sections.html:
Annual notices usually land between April 15 and July 1, and the 45 days to appeal are counted from the date printed on the notice. The department stresses that it cannot extend that date, and it recommends filing early and keeping your own copy in case the online system misbehaves.

You can post the form, hand it in at the annex, or use the online property search. A dropbox in the parking lot covers evenings. Faxed or emailed forms are turned away, and anyone filing for an owner needs a signed authorization letter.

Request your property record card, plus the comparable sales the county holds, before you commit to an appeal. Boats, aircraft and business equipment get a notice only if the value shifts or the county rejects a return filed in the first quarter.

sections.h2: How an appeal moves from the assessors to court
sections.html:
An appeal advances in stages, and you can stop at whichever stage gives you a fair number. The default track ends before a Board of Equalization seated by the grand jury.

  1. The assessors take a fresh look and mail a written answer, called the 30-day letter, that says whether the value changed.
  2. If the value holds, the file moves to the Board of Equalization automatically. If it drops and you are satisfied, the appeal lapses once the 30 days expire.
  3. If it changes and you still disagree, say so in writing before the 30 days end.
  4. The Board of Equalization mails notice of a hearing date, and the county recommends appearing with your own proof of market value.
  5. After the hearing, either side can take the result to Superior Court within 30 days of the mailing, and the owner pays a $25 filing fee at the court clerk's office.

Other routes open when you file. Arbitration looks at value alone. A hearing officer handles non-homestead parcels valued above $500,000 and rules on value and uniformity. Going to Superior Court directly needs the assessors' agreement and allows every kind of argument. The four grounds for appeal are taxability, value, uniformity and a denied exemption.

The Tax Commissioner takes homestead applications online and at the counter year-round, with April 1 as the cutoff for the cycle in progress. You must be both the owner and a resident as of January 1. Bring a state ID or driver's license plus a vehicle registration carrying the homestead address. A second window opens for the 45 days after a notice.

Exemption types the county offers:

  • The standard homestead exemption.
  • Age 62 and age 65 senior exemptions, plus a 65 fixed-income version with an income requirement.
  • Disability, supported by two kinds of proof or certificates from two doctors, with a Social Security Administration letter.
  • Disabled veteran, shown by a VA statement of service-connected benefits paid at 100 percent on January 1.
  • Surviving spouses of armed forces members killed in action, and of police officers or firefighters killed on duty.

Douglas is also among the counties with a valuation freeze, meaning a base-year figure holds the taxable value while the owner lives there. The Tax Commissioner can give the base year and the conditions.

The county has about 720 residents per land square mile across 200 square miles. Growth is 6.9 percent over the 2020 base, to an estimated 154,293 people, and 801 building permits were issued in 2025.

Because about two of every three occupied homes have an owner living in them, an assessment jump reaches many households at once. Set the value on your notice beside nearby sales before choosing to appeal. Owners without a mortgage report typical monthly costs of $507.

Under Georgia practice, ownership on January 1 fixes who owes for the year, and a later sale returns nothing to the seller. December 20 is the common due date, with a 60-day payment window. Douglas County's bill date and your parcel's balance come from the Tax Commissioner.

Check the commissioner's site for the delinquent list, upcoming tax sales and excess funds, which will show any unpaid earlier year. Liens from county taxes are recorded on the general execution docket at the clerk, and the commissioner can confirm whether your parcel has one.

Dividing a lot before you sell starts with a survey submitted to the Zoning Administrator. After the approved, stamped survey is recorded, new deeds are signed and filed with the clerk, while a deed specialist inside Appraisal updates the tax records. Heirs and delinquent owners sometimes pick a no-repair cash sale, with the tax paid at closing.

Before listing, pull your property record card and read the square footage, bedroom count and condition notes against what the house really has. Errors in the record are a common reason for an inflated value, and a buyer's agent will see the same card.

Next, ask the Tax Commissioner for a written balance and confirm your homestead status. If you applied for a senior or disability exemption, find out whether it carries over to the next owner. It does not follow the house automatically, so the buyer will need to apply on their own.

Finally, give the closing attorney the payoff figure so the tax is paid out of the proceeds. A cash buyer skips the lender's checklist, but the title search still turns up any open balance.

faqs.q: Does Douglas County take an appeal by fax or email?
faqs.a: No. Post it, bring it to the annex or use the online property search. If a representative files, include a letter of authorization.

faqs.q: How long do I have to appeal a Douglas County assessment?
faqs.a: You have 45 days from the date printed on the notice, and the department cannot extend that date. Notices usually arrive between April 15 and July 1.

faqs.q: How much is the Superior Court fee for a Douglas County appeal?
faqs.a: A $25 filing fee goes to the Clerk of Superior Court, and the owner tells the assessors in writing. Owner or assessors can appeal a Board of Equalization decision within 30 days of its mailing.

faqs.q: Where does a Douglas County homestead application go?
faqs.a: To the Tax Commissioner, either online or in person. Bring a state ID or driver's license and a vehicle registration showing the house address. You need to own and occupy the home on January 1, and April 1 is the usual cutoff.

faqs.q: If I sell in spring, who owes Douglas County's tax for the year?
faqs.a: The person who owned it on January 1 owes for all twelve months, with no partial-year refund from Georgia. Your contract and settlement statement divide the cost with the buyer, so ask the Tax Commissioner for the balance first.
